paragraphs: Plumi. (A Tanna of a baraita). In [Menachot 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.37a.7), [Plumi] asked Rabbi: one who has two heads, on which of them does he put tefillin? (In Hyman’s explanation, Rabbi thought he was asking in jest.) He said to him: Get up and go into exile, or accept excommunication upon yourself. Meanwhile a certain man came and told him that a child had been born to him with two heads. And he is mentioned in a baraita in [Berakhot 48b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.48b.13), after Rabbi

Yose, that Plumi says: one must put circumcision before Torah. And in [Pesachim 8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.8b.2), he said: A hole between a Jew’s and an Aramean’s premises need not be searched, because of danger. And in [Rosh Hashanah 24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.24a.14-15) he says: in its time one does not sanctify it, and he disputes with Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon [ראבר״ש]. And in [Sotah 4a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.4a.3-4) he disputes with Rabbi Elazar ben Yirmeya and Chanin ben Pinchas on the required duration of seclusion.

And in [Taanit 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.25a.8) a baraita quotes Plumi: “I saw that house, which Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa roofed through his prayer.” And Hyman tells a wondrous story about him in Kiddushin 91a (צא. in the supplied text; compare [81a:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81a.15) and [81b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.81b.1)): Plumi was accustomed to say every day, 'An arrow in the eye of the Satan' (in Hyman’s explanation, he was no longer afraid of the evil inclination). One day, on the eve of Yom Kippur, [Satan] appeared to him as a poor man, came and knocked at the door.[^7]

They brought him bread, and the poor man asked permission to eat at his table, and when he sat to eat he did disgusting things, and Plumi rebuked him and said to him: Sit properly. And the poor man made himself like a dead man, and a rumor went out that Plumi had killed a man, and Plumi fled to the place abbreviated בה״ב [compare the privy in Kiddushin 81b] and he [Satan] ran after him, and when he saw that he was very distressed he revealed himself to him that he was the Satan and had distressed him so that he would not be accustomed to say thus, 'An arrow
in the eye of the Satan.' But let him say from now on: May the Merciful rebuke the Satan.

The selected Davidson passages use Peleimo/Peleimu where Hyman supplies Plumi; the supplied name remains here. Menachot 37a has Peleimo asking Rabbi and the reply to go into exile or accept excommunication; the interpretation that Rabbi thought the question a joke is Hyman’s. Rosh Hashanah 24a spells out Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, supporting the local expansion of ראבר״ש, and Taanit 25a explicitly names Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa. The selected Sotah 4a paragraphs name Chanin ben Pinchas and Peleimo; they do not establish an expansion of the abbreviated title before Elazar ben Yirmeya. The abbreviated title before Yose in the Berakhot report also remains R'. The selected Kiddushin narrative starts on 81a and continues on 81b, where בית הכסא is explicit; these are positive comparisons beside the retained supplied צא. (91a) and בה״ב, not repairs to them. The story’s abridgment and explanation of fear of the evil inclination remain Hyman’s account. All three earlier mixed notes remain verbatim, including their earlier speculative alternatives, which are not restored as the translation. These named digital passages do not establish printed correction history or an independent identity, teacher, or chronological conclusion. Both source holds remain.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1011) has Plumi, cites Kiddushin 91a, and appears to abbreviate the place to which he fled as בה״ב, as in the supplied text. The corresponding account in the consulted Kiddushin runs from 81a to 81b and explicitly names the privy. The printed citation and supplied abbreviation are retained. Hyman abridges the dialogue, cup episode and flight, and the explanation that Plumi no longer feared the evil inclination is Hyman’s.

In Berakhot 48b–49a, Plumi’s ruling follows Rabbi Yose’s and concerns mentioning the covenant of circumcision before Torah in the blessing for the Land. The consulted Sotah 4a spells out Rabbi Elazar ben Yirmeya, then names Chanin ben Pinchas and Peleimu. These are local comparisons. In Rosh Hashanah 24a, Peleimu distinguishes the new moon seen at its expected time from one seen later, while Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon requires no formal sanctification in either case.

[Seder HaDorot 2956](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2956&lang=en) gives the story as beginning at the end of 81a and quotes the continuation, including the cup episode and the flight to the privy. At [Rosh Hashanah 24a:14–15](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.24a.14-15) Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok appears before Plumi’s ruling, and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon follows it. Hyman is comparing Plumi’s ruling with the latter.
